architecture_decisions.recommendation: Moved QL search from enterprise module to core API by integrating it into the default pagination class and filter backends
architecture_decisions.rationale: To make advanced search available to all users without enterprise license, the search functionality needed to be integrated into the core API stack. This involved modifying the default pagination to include autocomplete data and adding QLSearch as the primary filter backend instead of the basic SearchFilter.
alternatives_considered: Creating a new open source search module without modifying existing pagination

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Relocated search files from enterprise/search to api/search directory while preserving functionality
architecture_decisions.rationale: The search functionality is now a core API feature rather than an enterprise add-on. Moving files to the api directory makes logical sense for organization and clarifies that this is part of the public API surface. This maintains the same code structure but in a more appropriate location.
alternatives_considered: Keeping files in enterprise directory with feature flags
Creating completely new implementations in api directory

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created new schema module for autocomplete and moved schema post-processing hook
architecture_decisions.rationale: The autocomplete schema definition needed to be separated from the enterprise module. Creating a dedicated schema file in the v3 API structure follows the existing pattern of organizing OpenAPI schema components. This ensures proper OpenAPI documentation generation for the new autocomplete field.
alternatives_considered: Keeping schema definition in the ql.py file

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed enterprise search app from settings and updated client SDKs to reflect the change
architecture_decisions.rationale: Since search is no longer an enterprise feature, it needed to be removed from enterprise app registration and client SDK enums. This prevents confusion about feature availability and ensures consistent behavior across all client libraries.
alternatives_considered: Keeping enterprise search as deprecated module

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated paginated response models to include autocomplete field as required property
architecture_decisions.rationale: All paginated API responses now include autocomplete data for QL search. This required updating the response schema in OpenAPI definitions and client SDK models to include the new field as required, ensuring type safety and proper documentation.
alternatives_considered: Creating separate response types for search-enabled endpoints

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Moved and simplified search tests by removing enterprise mocking
architecture_decisions.rationale: Tests needed to be relocated to the api module and simplified since they no longer require enterprise feature flags. The test now validates core functionality without enterprise dependencies, ensuring the feature works in the open source context.
alternatives_considered: Keeping tests in enterprise module with modified mocking
Creating new test suite from scratch

implementation_summary:
The implementation moves the advanced query language (QL) search functionality from the enterprise module to the open source codebase through a systematic refactoring approach. The core strategy involved relocating search-related files from the enterprise/search directory to api/search while preserving their functionality, then integrating QL search into the default API infrastructure.

Key architectural changes include modifying the base Pagination class to automatically include autocomplete data in all paginated responses, and configuring QLSearch as the default filter backend in Django REST Framework settings. This ensures that all API endpoints automatically gain QL search capabilities without requiring individual endpoint modifications. The autocomplete schema was extracted into a dedicated module (api/v3/schema/search.py) following the existing schema organization pattern.

All enterprise dependencies were removed from view files by importing search components directly from the new api.search module instead of enterprise.search. Client SDKs were regenerated to include the new required autocomplete field in paginated response models and to remove enterprise.search from the app enumeration. The implementation maintains backward compatibility for existing API consumers while adding the enhanced search functionality transparently.

This approach successfully democratizes advanced event log searching by making it available to all authentik users without requiring an enterprise license, while maintaining code organization and following established patterns within the Django monolith architecture.
